description.value: A very large solenoid magnet, later reused as ALICE's central magnet at the same LEP/LHC point.

summary.plain: A detector at LEP's Point 2 built to measure electrons, muons and photons with exceptional precision, using dense bismuth-germanate crystals and one of the largest magnets ever built for a particle detector.
summary.technical: L3-optimised (not fully general-purpose) LEP detector: silicon-strip microvertex detector and time-expansion chamber for tracking, a bismuth-germanate (BGO) electromagnetic calorimeter, a hadron calorimeter, a muon spectrometer and scintillation counters, all inside a very large solenoid magnet. That magnet was left in place after LEP shut down and now forms the core of the ALICE detector at the same point.

technology.locator: 'The Construction of the L3 Experiment', Nucl.Instrum.Meth.A 289 (1990) 35, abstract
technology.quote: It is the only detector that concentrates its efforts on limited goals of measuring electrons, muons and photons.
technology.value: Collider detector optimised for high-resolution electron, muon and photon measurement, built around a bismuth-germanate calorimeter and a very large solenoid magnet
